lines.ja: あった。{でも、}夜は寒くて、長く入れなかった。
lines.en: There was. But it was cold at night, so I couldn't stay in long.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あー、}十一月だもんね。料理は？
lines.en: Ah, it is November. What about the food?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 料理が一番よかった！魚がすごくおいしくて。
lines.en: The food was the best part! The fish was amazing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {いくら、あ、}高かった？
lines.en: How much... oh, was it expensive?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {えっと、}一泊一万五千円。{まあ、}ちょっと高いけど。
lines.en: Um, fifteen thousand yen a night. A bit pricey, I guess.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {でも、}いいね。今度、場所教えて。
lines.en: Still, sounds good. Tell me where it is sometime.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うん、あとで地図、送るね。
lines.en: Sure, I'll send you a map later.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あのさ、}前に言ってたルームシェアの話、{まあ、}本気で考えてみたんだけど。
lines.en: So, about that flat-share idea we talked about, I've actually been thinking about it seriously.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: うん。
lines.en: Uh-huh.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 家賃、今一人で七万払ってるじゃん。二人なら{その、}一人五万くらいで、もっと広いとこ住めるなって。
lines.en: I'm paying seventy thousand in rent on my own right now. With two of us it'd be about fifty each, and we could get somewhere bigger.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うーん、}お金は助かるんだけど…{なんか}俺、朝めっちゃ早いじゃん。五時とかに起きるし。
lines.en: Hmm, the money would help, but… I get up really early, you know. Like five o'clock.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 知ってる。でも私、夜型だから、逆にちょうどいいかなって。お風呂もキッチンも、使う時間がかぶらないし。
lines.en: I know. But I'm a night owl, so I figure that actually works. We'd never need the bath or the kitchen at the same time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: あー、そういう考え方もあるか。
lines.en: Ah, I guess that's one way to see it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: でしょ？ {で、}問題は家事なんだよね。拓海、{その、}片付けとか…
lines.en: Right? So the real problem is housework. Takumi, tidying up and stuff…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いや、するよ？ するする。{た、}たまに。
lines.en: Hey, I do it! I do. …Sometimes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ほら、それ。だから当番表作ろうよ。週ごとに交代で。
lines.en: See, that. So let's make a chore rota. We swap every week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うーん、}当番表か…{まあ、}それならいいけど。あ、でも一個だけ条件ある。
lines.en: Hmm, a rota… Well, that's fine. Oh, but I've got one condition.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: なに？
lines.en: What?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 友達呼ぶときは、前の日までに言うこと。急に来られるの、{なんか}落ち着かないんだよね。
lines.en: If you have friends over, tell me by the day before. People turning up out of nowhere kind of stresses me out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それは全然いいよ。{じゃあ、}来月、一緒に物件見に行く？
lines.en: That's totally fine. So, want to go look at some places together next month?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うん、}行こ行こ。{あ、}でも契約はまだ決めないからね。見るだけ。
lines.en: Yeah, let's go. Oh, but I'm not signing anything yet. Just looking.

dialogues.title: The first date that went wrong

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}聞いてよ。昨日の初デート、もう最悪だった。
lines.en: Listen to this. My first date yesterday was an absolute disaster.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、マジで？ 何があったの？
lines.en: Wait, seriously? What happened?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {えっと、}まず、予約してたレストランが、{その、}店の工事で休みだったの。
lines.en: Well, first, the restaurant I'd booked was closed for building work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: うわ。
lines.en: Oof.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: で、しょうがないから近くのラーメン屋入ったんだけど、彼女、{なんか}白い服着てて…
lines.en: So we had no choice and went into a ramen place nearby, but she was wearing, like, a white outfit…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: あー、スープ飛んだ？
lines.en: Ah, soup splashed?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 飛んだ。しかも俺のじゃなくて、隣のおじさんの。
lines.en: It did. And not from mine — from the guy sitting next to us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {え、}ちょっと待って、それ翔太のせいじゃないじゃん。
lines.en: Wait a sec, that's not even your fault.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうなんだけど、{まあ、}空気がね…で、帰りに{雨、あ、}大雨が降ってきて、傘一本しかなくて。
lines.en: I know, but the mood… And then on the way back it started pouring, and we only had one umbrella.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、それ逆にいい感じじゃない？ 相合傘でしょ？
lines.en: Hey, isn't that actually kind of nice? Sharing an umbrella?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}俺もそう思ったんだけど、{その、}彼女が『私は走るから大丈夫』って、駅まで走ってっちゃった。
lines.en: That's what I thought too, but she said 'I'll just run, it's fine' and ran off to the station.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うーん、}それは…{なんか}照れてただけかもよ？ その後、連絡は？
lines.en: Hmm, maybe she was just shy? Did you hear from her after?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {それが、}今朝メッセージが来て、『昨日は楽しかったです、また行きましょう』って。
lines.en: Well, this morning she messaged me: 'I had fun yesterday, let's go again.'

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、じゃあ全然最悪じゃないじゃん！
lines.en: Then it wasn't a disaster at all!

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {まあ、}そうなんだよね。だから次は、ちゃんと天気予報見てから誘うわ。
lines.en: Yeah, I guess so. So next time I'll check the weather forecast before I ask her out.

questions.question: Why did they end up eating ramen?
choices: The restaurant was fully booked
The place he had reserved was shut
She said she wanted something cheap
It was raining too hard to go far

choices: She was angry about her clothes
She had a train to catch

choices: She wants to see him again

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あのさ、}お正月のことなんだけど、そろそろ決めないと。
lines.en: So, about New Year — we really need to decide.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: あ、そうだね。新幹線の切符、早く取らないと高くなるし。
lines.en: Oh, right. Bullet train tickets get pricier if we don't book early.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {で、}去年はうちの実家だったじゃん。だから今年は、{まあ、}普通に考えたら奈々の実家かなって。
lines.en: Last year we went to my parents'. So this year, normally, it'd be your parents' place.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うーん、}それがね…うちの母が、{なんか}今年は旅行に行くって言ってて。
lines.en: Hmm, well… my mum says she's going on a trip this year.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: え、お正月に？
lines.en: What, over New Year?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そう、父と二人で温泉だって。だから、うちに帰っても誰もいないの。
lines.en: Yeah, a hot spring with my dad, just the two of them. So there'd be nobody home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: なるほど。{じゃあ、}また俺の実家？ {いや、}うちの親は喜ぶと思うけど、二年連続は疲れない？
lines.en: I see. So my parents' again? I mean, they'd be happy, but wouldn't two years in a row wear you out?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {まあ、}正直ちょっとね。お義母さん優しいけど、ずっと気を使うし。
lines.en: Honestly, a bit. Your mum's lovely, but I'm on my best behaviour the whole time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: だよね。{じゃあ、}こういうのは？ 元日だけうちの実家に顔出して、二日からは二人でどっか行くの。
lines.en: Figured. So how about this: we drop by my parents' just on New Year's Day, and from the second we go somewhere, just us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: あ、それいい！ {えっと、}遠くじゃなくて、近場の温泉とか？
lines.en: Oh, I like that! Not far, maybe a hot spring nearby?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうそう。うちの親も、一日会えれば満足すると思うし。
lines.en: Exactly. My parents will be happy enough seeing us for a day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {じゃあ、}私、今夜宿調べとくね。大輔はお母さんに電話しといて。
lines.en: Then I'll look up places to stay tonight. You call your mum.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 了解。{あ、}お土産も何か考えなきゃな。
lines.en: Got it. Oh, we'll need to think of a gift to bring, too.

dialogues.title: A farewell party on a budget

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {えっと、}山田さんの送別会なんだけど、予算、一人三千円でって言われちゃって。
lines.en: So, about Yamada-san's farewell party — they told us the budget is three thousand yen a head.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 三千円ですか。{うーん、}飲み放題つけたら、それだけで終わっちゃいますね。
lines.en: Three thousand? Hmm, an all-you-can-drink plan would eat that up by itself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうなのよ。{で、}花束も買わなきゃいけないし。
lines.en: Exactly. And we need to buy flowers too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あの、}会社の会議室でやるのはどうですか？ 料理は{その、}ケータリング頼んで。
lines.en: What about doing it in a meeting room at work? We could get the food catered.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あー、}会議室か。でも山田さん、お酒好きじゃない？ 会社だと飲めないし…
lines.en: Ah, a meeting room. But Yamada-san loves a drink, doesn't she? We can't drink at the office…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: あ、そっか。
lines.en: Oh, right.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {なんか}寂しい感じになっちゃうかなって。
lines.en: I feel like it'd end up a bit sad.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {じゃあ、}駅前の居酒屋はどうですか？ 平日なら個室が安くなるって聞きましたよ。
lines.en: Then how about the izakaya by the station? I heard their private rooms are cheaper on weekdays.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: え、ほんと？ 山田さんの最後の日、金曜だよね。
lines.en: Really? Her last day's a Friday, isn't it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {金曜は、あ、}金曜はダメかもしれません。安いのは月曜から木曜だけで…
lines.en: Friday might not work. The discount's only Monday to Thursday…

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {じゃあ、}木曜にしよう。最終日の前の日のほうが、{まあ、}本人もゆっくりできるし。
lines.en: Then let's do Thursday. The day before her last day, she can relax more anyway.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうですね。花束は、{その、}予算から出します？
lines.en: Makes sense. Do we take the flowers out of the budget?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ううん、花束は別で、一人五百円ずつ集めよう。森くん、居酒屋の予約お願いできる？
lines.en: No, let's collect five hundred yen each separately for the flowers. Mori-kun, could you book the izakaya?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい、今日中に電話しときます。
lines.en: Sure, I'll call them today.

questions.question: Why is Kobayashi unenthusiastic about the meeting room?

Yamada couldn't enjoy a drink there
It's too small for the whole team
It's already booked on Friday

choices: Yamada is busy on her last day
Mori can only phone on Thursday

Mori will pay and be repaid later

speakers.name: 高橋
speakers.hint: polite-casual, a little anxious about cost

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: すみません、{あの、}この自転車なんですけど、ブレーキから{なんか}変な音がして…
lines.en: Excuse me, it's this bike — the brakes are making a strange noise…

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はいはい、ちょっと見せてくださいね。{うーん、}{あー、}これはブレーキだけじゃないなあ。
lines.en: Sure, let me have a look. Hmm… ah, it's not just the brakes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、そうなんですか？
lines.en: Oh, really?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: チェーンも錆びてるし、タイヤも前後ともだいぶ減ってますね。全部直すと、{まあ、}一万五千円くらいかな。
lines.en: The chain's rusty, and both tyres, front and back, are pretty worn. Fixing everything would be about fifteen thousand.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 一万五千…{えっと、}新しいのって、いくらぐらいします？
lines.en: Fifteen thousand… um, how much is a new one?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 安いのなら二万ちょっとからありますよ。{ただ、}{その、}お客さんのこれ、フレームはいいやつなんですよ。
lines.en: Cheap ones start at a bit over twenty thousand. But this one of yours, the frame's a really good one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: あ、これ、父からもらったんです。もう十年以上乗ってて。
lines.en: Oh, my father gave it to me. I've been riding it over ten years.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: なるほどね。{いや、}大事に乗ってたんだなって、見れば分かりますよ。
lines.en: I see. I can tell you've looked after it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うーん、}でも正直、通勤で毎日使うんで、また壊れたら困るなって。
lines.en: Hmm, but honestly, I use it every day to get to work, so I'd be stuck if it broke again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ちゃんと直せば、あと五年は大丈夫ですよ。安い新品より長持ちすると思いますけどね。
lines.en: Fix it properly and it'll be fine for another five years. I'd say it'll outlast a cheap new one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうなんですね。{じゃあ、}直してもらおうかな。{あ、}何日くらいかかります？
lines.en: I see. Then I'll get it fixed. Oh, how many days will it take?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 部品を取り寄せるんで、{えっと、}木曜の夕方ですね。
lines.en: I have to order parts, so… Thursday evening.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 木曜か…{その、}通勤どうしよう。
lines.en: Thursday… how will I get to work, though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あ、}よかったら、うちの貸し自転車使ってください。お代はいいですから。
lines.en: Oh, if you like, use one of our loan bikes. No charge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、いいんですか？ 助かります！
lines.en: Really? That's a big help!

questions.question: Why does the owner lean towards repairing the bike?
choices: A new bike would take longer to arrive
The repair costs under half the new price
Her father asked him to keep it running
Its frame is good enough to outlast a cheap bike

questions.question: What was the customer's main concern?
choices: Being stuck if it broke down again
Upsetting her father by replacing it

Not having time to bring it back

By buying a cheap new bike

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あ、}もしもし、里美？ {えっと、}俺、和也。高校の…
lines.en: Hello, Satomi? Um, it's me, Kazuya. From high school…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、和也？ うそ、久しぶり！ 何年ぶり？
lines.en: Kazuya? No way, it's been ages! How many years?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {たぶん、}卒業以来だから…十二年？ {いや、}十三年か。
lines.en: Since graduation, so… twelve years? No, thirteen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: えー、そんなに！ {で、}どうしたの急に？
lines.en: Wow, that long! So what's up, out of the blue?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}{その、}実は来月、仕事でそっちに転勤になって。
lines.en: Well, actually, I'm being transferred to your area for work next month.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: へえ！
lines.en: Oh wow!

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: で、そっちに知り合い、里美しかいなくてさ。{まあ、}ちょっと心細くて、電話しちゃった。
lines.en: And you're the only person I know there. I felt a bit lost, so I called.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: なにそれ、全然いいよ。{あ、}でも私、今は市内じゃなくて、{えっと、}ちょっと離れた町に住んでるんだよね。
lines.en: Don't be silly, that's fine. Oh, but I don't live in the city now — I'm in a town a bit further out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: あ、そうなんだ。
lines.en: Oh, really.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: うん。結婚して、子どもが生まれてから引っ越したの。
lines.en: Yeah. I got married, and we moved after the baby was born.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: え、結婚したの！ おめでとう。{いや、}ほんと、{なんか}時間経ってるな。
lines.en: You got married! Congratulations. Wow, a lot of time really has passed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: でしょ？ {じゃあ、}引っ越しが落ち着いたら、うちにご飯食べに来てよ。夫も喜ぶと思う。
lines.en: Right? So once you've settled in, come over for dinner. My husband would love it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: いいの？ {じゃあ、}お言葉に甘えて。{あ、}俺の番号、登録しといて。
lines.en: Really? Then I'll take you up on it. Oh, save my number.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 了解。{あ、}そうだ、高校のみんなにも声かけてみようか？
lines.en: Will do. Oh, I know — shall I get in touch with the others from school too?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}それはまた今度で。まずは{その、}新しい生活に慣れてからかな。
lines.en: Nah, maybe another time. I think I'll get used to my new life first.

questions.question: Why did Kazuya call Satomi now?
choices: He wants to organise a school reunion
He heard she had got married
He is looking for a job near her town
He's moving to her area and knows nobody else

He isn't interested in seeing them

speakers.name: 翼
speakers.hint: frustrated, apologetic, casual-polite to an older teammate

speakers.name: 大樹
speakers.hint: calm team captain, gruff but kind

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}悔しいっすね。三対二って、{なんか}勝てた試合でしたよ。
lines.en: Man, that stings. Three–two… we could've won that game.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {まあ、}な。前半は完全にうちのペースだったしな。
lines.en: Yeah. The first half was totally ours.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうそう。
lines.en: Exactly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: でも後半、みんな足止まってたろ。{正直、}体力の問題だと思うよ。
lines.en: But in the second half everyone's legs went. Honestly, I think it's about fitness.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あー、}俺も最後、全然走れなかったです。{あの、}二点目は、{俺の、}完全に俺のミスで…
lines.en: Yeah, I couldn't run at all by the end. And the second goal, that was totally my mistake…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {いや、}あれは一人のせいじゃないって。
lines.en: Nah, that wasn't down to one person.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: でも…
lines.en: But…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: それより、次どうするか考えようぜ。練習、週二回に増やすか？
lines.en: More importantly, let's think about next time. Should we go up to two practices a week?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {うーん、}二回はきつい人もいると思います。仕事ある人多いし。
lines.en: Hmm, twice would be tough for some people. Lots of them have jobs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: だよな。{じゃあ、}練習は週一のままで、最初の三十分、走るメニュー入れるか。
lines.en: True. Then we keep it at once a week, and put running drills in the first thirty minutes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: あ、それいいっすね。あと、交代ももっと早めにしたほうがいいかなって。
lines.en: Oh, that's good. And I reckon we should make substitutions earlier, too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 確かに。今日、ベンチのやつ、ほとんど出てなかったもんな。
lines.en: True. The guys on the bench hardly played today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {はい、}{その、}次の試合、再来週ですよね。それまでに{なんか}…
lines.en: Yeah, the next game's the week after next, right? Before then we should…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: おう。{じゃ、}とりあえず今日はラーメン行こうぜ。反省会はそこで。
lines.en: Yeah. Anyway, let's go for ramen today. We'll do the post-mortem there.

They ran out of energy in the second half
The substitutes came on too late
They only practise once a week

Adding a practice match before the next game
Starting each weekly session with running
Spending time reviewing mistakes after training

He's annoyed that the bench didn't play

speakers.name: 沙織

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {ねえ、}今月の電気代、見た？ {なんか}すごいことになってるんだけど。
lines.en: Hey, did you see this month's electricity bill? It's kind of crazy.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 見た見た。一万二千円でしょ。{まあ、}エアコン毎日つけてたしね。
lines.en: Yeah, I saw. Twelve thousand, right? Well, we had the air-con on every day.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {で、}{その、}言いにくいんだけど…真紀さん、在宅で、昼間もずっとエアコン使ってるじゃない？
lines.en: So, um, this is awkward, but… you work from home, and you use the air-con all day too, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あー、}うん、それはそうだね。
lines.en: Ah, yeah, that's true.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: だから、半分ずつっていうのは{ちょっと}…{なんか}私ばっかり損してる気がして。
lines.en: So splitting it half and half feels… like I'm the one losing out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 分かる。{えっと、}じゃあ、どうしようか。私が七割とか？
lines.en: I get it. So what should we do? I pay seventy percent?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}七割は多すぎるよ。夜は私も使ってるし。
lines.en: No, seventy's too much. I use it at night too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {じゃあ、}六割。で、ガス代と水道代は、今まで通り半分ずつ。
lines.en: Then sixty. And gas and water stay half each, like before.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うん、それなら{まあ、}公平かなって。{あ、}ネット代は？
lines.en: Yeah, that seems fair. Oh, what about the internet?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ネットは、{その、}仕事で使ってるの私だから、私が全部払うよ。
lines.en: The internet — I'm the one using it for work, so I'll pay all of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: え、いいの？ {なんか}逆に悪いな。
lines.en: Really? Now I feel bad the other way.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いいっていいって。その代わり、お風呂掃除、ちょっと多めにお願いしてもいい？
lines.en: It's fine, it's fine. In return, could you do the bath cleaning a bit more often?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あ、}はい、喜んで。
lines.en: Oh, sure, happily.

questions.question: Why does Saori think an even split of the electricity is unfair?

Maki runs the air conditioner all day at home
The bill rose because of the internet
Maki pays less for gas and water

questions.question: How will they share the electricity bill from now on?
choices: Half each, as before
Maki pays seventy percent
Maki pays all of it
Maki pays sixty percent

questions.question: What does Maki ask for in return?
choices: That Saori clean the bath more often
That Saori use less air conditioning
That Saori pay the water bill
That Saori pay part of the internet

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {で、}田中の結婚祝い、何にする？ {なんか}二人で一緒に買おうって話だったよね。
lines.en: So, what are we getting Tanaka for the wedding? We said we'd buy something together, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: うん。予算は一人一万くらいで{いいかな、}いいよね？
lines.en: Yeah. About ten thousand each for the budget — that's fine, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うん。{えっと、}俺はさ、{その、}ペアのグラスとかどうかなって。
lines.en: Yeah. I was thinking maybe a pair of glasses?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あー、}グラスね。でもグラスって、けっこうもらうらしいよ。うちの姉も、結婚したとき五つぐらいもらったって。
lines.en: Ah, glasses. But apparently people get loads of those. My sister got about five sets when she got married.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: マジで？
lines.en: Seriously?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: マジで。{だから、なんか}かぶらないもののほうがいいかなって。
lines.en: Seriously. So I think something they won't get twice would be better.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {じゃあ、}カタログギフト？ 好きなもの選べるし。
lines.en: A catalogue gift, then? They can pick what they like.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うーん、}それは{ちょっと}味気なくない？ せっかく友達なんだし。
lines.en: Hmm, isn't that a bit impersonal? We're his friends, after all.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あ、}そういえば、田中、前にコーヒーにはまってるって言ってたな。{毎朝、あ、}休みの日は毎朝、豆から挽いてるって。
lines.en: Oh, come to think of it, Tanaka said he's into coffee. On his days off he grinds the beans himself every morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、それいいじゃん！ {じゃあ、}ちょっといいコーヒーメーカーは？
lines.en: Oh, that's great! So how about a nice coffee maker?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}そこまでやってるなら、もう持ってるんじゃない？
lines.en: Nah, if he's that into it, he probably already has one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あー、}確かに。{じゃあ、}ペアのマグカップと、珍しい豆のセットは？ それなら、かぶっても困らないし。
lines.en: Ah, true. Then how about matching mugs and a set of unusual beans? Even if someone else gives beans, it's no problem.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: いいね、それ。{じゃあ、}週末、駅前のコーヒー屋さん見に行こうか。
lines.en: Nice. Let's go check out the coffee shop by the station at the weekend.

questions.question: Why does Aya reject the glasses?

Couples tend to receive lots of them
Tanaka already has some
Her sister gave glasses and regretted it

questions.question: Why do they drop the coffee maker idea?
choices: Tanaka most likely owns one already
It costs more than ten thousand yen
It feels too impersonal
Tanaka only drinks coffee on days off

questions.question: What do they decide to buy?
choices: A catalogue gift
A pair of glasses and some beans
A coffee maker
Mugs and a selection of rare beans

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {ねえ、}前に作ってた刺繍のブローチ、{その、}ネットで売ってみようかなって思ってて。
lines.en: Hey, those embroidered brooches I was making — I'm thinking of trying to sell them online.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: へえ、いいじゃん。あれ、すごくきれいだったし。
lines.en: Oh, nice. They were really pretty.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: でも{なんか}、値段のつけ方が全然分からなくて。材料は一個三百円くらいなんだけど。
lines.en: But I have no idea how to price them. The materials are about three hundred yen each.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うーん、}作るのにどれくらいかかるの？
lines.en: Hmm, how long does one take to make?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {えっと、}一個二時間くらい？
lines.en: Um, about two hours each?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 二時間！ {じゃあ、}千円とかで売ったら、{その、}時給にしたら全然だよ。
lines.en: Two hours! Then if you sell them for a thousand, that's nothing as an hourly wage.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうなんだけど、高くしたら売れないかなって。
lines.en: I know, but I worry they won't sell if they're expensive.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {いや、}手作りのって、安すぎると逆に{なんか}安っぽく見えるらしいよ。二千五百円ぐらいでもいいんじゃない？
lines.en: Actually, they say if handmade stuff is too cheap it looks tacky. Couldn't you charge around two and a half thousand?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 二千五百円か…{まあ、}最初はちょっと勇気いるな。
lines.en: Two and a half thousand… that takes some nerve at first.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あ、}そうだ、写真。{写真が、あ、}ネットは写真で決まるからさ、俺、カメラ貸そうか？
lines.en: Oh, right, photos. Online it's all about the photos, so want to borrow my camera?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: え、ほんと？ 助かる！
lines.en: Really? That'd be great!

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ただ、最初からあんまり数作りすぎないほうがいいよ。在庫になると困るし。
lines.en: But don't make too many at first. You don't want to be stuck with stock.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {うん、}{じゃあ、}とりあえず十個だけ作って、二千円で出してみる。売れたら値段上げればいいし。
lines.en: OK, then I'll make just ten for now and list them at two thousand. If they sell, I can raise the price.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: おう、いいと思う。{あ、}最初の一個は俺が買うからね。
lines.en: Yeah, sounds good. Oh, and I'm buying the first one.

questions.question: What price does Keiko decide to start with?

Two thousand five hundred, as Koji said
Three hundred plus the cost of her time
Two thousand, with a rise if they sell

questions.question: Why does Koji think pricing too low is a mistake?
choices: It can make handmade goods look cheap
It wouldn't cover the materials
Other sellers would copy her designs
Buyers would expect larger orders

questions.question: What does Koji offer to do?
choices: Buy the first ten brooches
Lend her his camera
Keep her unsold stock
Make some of the brooches

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {ねえ、}聞いた？ 来月から営業と企画、統合されるらしいよ。
lines.en: Hey, did you hear? Apparently sales and planning are being merged from next month.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あー、}噂にはなってたけど、本当だったんだ。
lines.en: Ah, there were rumours, but it's actually true, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {うん、}{なんか}今朝、部長が{その、}ちょっと深刻な顔で会議室に入ってったから、{たぶん}それかなって。
lines.en: Yeah, this morning the department head went into the meeting room looking pretty serious, so I figured that's it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {え、}じゃあ、上田課長は？ 課長が二人になっちゃうじゃん。
lines.en: Wait, then what about Ueda, our section chief? We'd have two chiefs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そこなのよ。{まあ、}上田さん、前から海外の新規事業やりたいって言ってたから、{もしかしたら}そっちに行くのかもって。
lines.en: That's the thing. Well, Ueda-san has always said she wanted to do the new overseas business, so maybe she'll move there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: へえ、それなら本人的には、むしろ希望通りじゃない？
lines.en: Huh, then for her that's actually what she wanted, isn't it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうそう。
lines.en: Exactly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ただ、俺らの仕事の{やり方、}進め方はけっこう変わりそうだよね。企画の人たちって、{なんか}資料すごい細かいし。
lines.en: But how we do our work is probably going to change a lot. The planning people are super detailed with their documents.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {うーん、}それは慣れかな。むしろ営業の現場の声が企画に直接届くようになるのは、悪くないと思うけどな。
lines.en: Hmm, you'll get used to that. If anything, having the voices from the sales floor reach planning directly doesn't seem bad to me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 確かにね。{まあ、}正直、誰が上に来るかで全然違うけどね。
lines.en: True. Though honestly, it all depends on who ends up above us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あ、}それ、{その、}企画の森さんじゃないかって話もあるよ。
lines.en: Oh, there's talk it might be Mori-san from planning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、森さん？ あの人なら{まあ、}話分かるし、安心かも。
lines.en: Mori-san? She's reasonable, so that might be reassuring.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ただ、これ、まだ正式発表の前だから、{ね、}ここだけの話で。
lines.en: But this is before the official announcement, so keep it between us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 分かってるって。{あ、}{やば、}会議始まる。
lines.en: I know, I know. Oh, shoot, the meeting's starting.

questions.question: How does Nakamura see Ueda's possible move?
choices: As a demotion she'll resent
As a sign she'll lead the merged team
As a way to avoid having two chiefs for ever
As probably what she wanted anyway

questions.question: What is Sasaki's overall view of the merger?
choices: Mildly positive about sales feedback reaching planning
Worried about planning's detailed paperwork
Anxious because the department head looked serious
Opposed unless Mori becomes the new boss

questions.question: What does Sasaki ask Nakamura to do?
choices: Ask the department head directly
Keep it quiet until it's announced
Tell Mori about the rumour
Get to the meeting early

speakers.name: 石井
speakers.hint: earnest university student, polite to her senpai, anxious

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 先輩、{あの、}今ちょっとだけいいですか？ 就活のことで相談があって。
lines.en: Senpai, um, do you have a minute? I wanted to ask your advice about job hunting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: おう、いいよ。どうした？
lines.en: Sure. What's up?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {えっと、}{その、}志望業界がまだ決まってなくて。周りはもうインターンとか行ってるのに、{なんか}焦っちゃって。
lines.en: Well, I still haven't decided which industry I want. Everyone around me is already doing internships, and I'm panicking.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あー、}分かる分かる。{俺も、}俺も三年の夏はそんな感じだったよ。
lines.en: Ah, I get it. I was the same in the summer of third year.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: え、先輩もですか？
lines.en: Really, you too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: うん。で、そのときにやってよかったのが、{業界を、あ、}業界を絞る前に、自分が何をしてるときに楽しいかを書き出すこと。
lines.en: Yeah. And what helped me then was, before narrowing down industries, writing out what I'm doing when I'm enjoying myself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: なるほど。
lines.en: I see.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あと、}インターンは{まあ、}数じゃないから。一つ行って合わなかったら、それも収穫だし。
lines.en: And internships aren't about numbers. If you do one and it doesn't suit you, that's still something gained.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: でも、{その、}エントリーシートに書くことがなくて…サークルも途中でやめちゃったし。
lines.en: But I've got nothing to write on my application forms… I even quit my club halfway.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {いや、}やめた理由をちゃんと説明できれば、マイナスにはならないよ。{むしろ}何を考えて決めたかのほうが見られてるから。
lines.en: No, if you can properly explain why you quit, it won't count against you. They look more at how you thought it through.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうなんですね…{なんか}ちょっと気が楽になりました。
lines.en: Oh, really… I feel a bit better now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {じゃあ、}今度、うちの会社の説明会あるから、よかったら来る？ 雰囲気だけでも。
lines.en: Well, my company has an information session soon — want to come? Even just to get a feel for it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: え、いいんですか！ ぜひ行きたいです。
lines.en: Really? I'd love to go.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: おう。{じゃ、}日程、あとで送るわ。
lines.en: Sure. I'll send you the dates later.

questions.question: What does Okada recommend doing before choosing an industry?
choices: Signing up for as many internships as possible
Listing the activities she enjoys
Asking friends which industries they chose
Attending company information sessions

questions.question: What is Okada's view of Ishii quitting her club?
choices: She should leave it off her forms
It shows a lack of commitment
It's fine if she explains her reasoning
She should write about internships instead

questions.question: How does Ishii feel by the end?
choices: Less pressured than before
Still behind everyone else
Worried about her entry sheet
Unsure whether to go to the session

dialogues.title: To cram or not to cram

speakers.name: 井上
speakers.hint: friendly mother, polite-casual, a little worried

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あの、}西村さんのところって、もう塾、行かせてます？
lines.en: Um, Nishimura-san, have you started sending your kid to cram school yet?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うーん、}それがまだなんですよ。{妻とも、}妻とも話してるんですけど、{なんか}決めきれなくて。
lines.en: Hmm, not yet, actually. I've been talking it over with my wife, but we can't quite decide.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うちもなんです。クラスの半分くらいはもう通ってるって、{その、}子どもが言うんですよね。
lines.en: Same here. My kid says about half the class goes already.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あー、}うちも言われました。『みんな行ってる』って。
lines.en: Ah, we heard that too. 'Everyone goes.'

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうそう。
lines.en: Right, right.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {でも、}正直、週三回で月三万って、なかなかですよね。
lines.en: But honestly, thirty thousand a month for three times a week is a lot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: それに、本人が本当に行きたいのかっていうのも、{なんか}気になってて。うちの子、サッカーも続けたいって言ってるんですよ。
lines.en: And I'm also not sure whether he really wants to go. My son says he wants to keep up football too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: あー、分かります。
lines.en: Oh, I understand.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {だから、}{まあ、}とりあえず夏期講習だけ行かせてみようかなって。合わなかったらやめればいいし。
lines.en: So, I'm thinking of just trying the summer course for now. If it doesn't suit him, he can stop.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あ、}それいいですね。お試しみたいな感じで。
lines.en: Oh, that's a good idea. Like a trial.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ええ。{あと、}{その、}駅前の塾は、授業の前に自習室が使えるらしくて。
lines.en: Yes. Also, apparently the one by the station lets kids use a study room before class.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: へえ、それは助かりますね。{家だと、}家だとどうしてもスマホ見ちゃうから。
lines.en: Oh, that's helpful. At home they always end up looking at their phones.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ですよね。{じゃあ、}今度一緒に説明会に行ってみます？
lines.en: Exactly. Then shall we go to an information session together sometime?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ぜひ。{あ、}でも夏期講習の申し込み、{たしか、}今月末までだったような…
lines.en: Definitely. Oh, but I think the summer course sign-up closes at the end of this month…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、そうなんですか。{じゃあ、}のんびりしてられないですね。
lines.en: Oh, is that right? Then we can't take our time.

questions.question: What does Nishimura plan to do?
choices: Enrol his son three times a week
Wait until his son gives up football
Let his son try a short course first
Choose whichever school classmates attend

choices: Doubt that his son really wants to go

Worry that half the class is ahead

choices: The information session is this month
The study room is only for enrolled students
The summer course is already full
They need to decide soon because of a deadline

dialogues.title: A polite word about the noise

speakers.name: 松本
speakers.hint: apologetic, sincere, keen to fix it

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あの、}夜分にすみません。下の階の田村と申します。
lines.en: Excuse me for calling so late. I'm Tamura, from the floor below.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: あ、はい。{えっと、}何か…
lines.en: Oh, yes. Um, is something…

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}{その、}大したことじゃないんですが、最近、夜の十一時過ぎぐらいに、ドンドンって音が響くことがありまして。
lines.en: Oh, it's nothing serious, but recently, sometime after eleven at night, there's been a thumping sound coming through.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: あ、すみません！ {えっと、}たぶん息子だと思います。まだ三歳で、夜なかなか寝なくて…
lines.en: Oh, I'm so sorry! That's probably my son. He's only three, and he won't settle at night…

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ああ、なるほど。
lines.en: Ah, I see.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}お子さんなら仕方ないですよ。{ただ、}私、朝が早い仕事なもので、{その、}できれば十時以降だけでも、少し気をつけていただけると…
lines.en: Well, with a small child it can't be helped. It's just that I start work early, so if you could take a little care, even just after ten…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: もちろんです。気づかなくて、本当に申し訳ありません。{あの、}実は、リビングに防音のマットを敷こうかって、ちょうど夫と話してたところなんです。
lines.en: Of course. I'm really sorry I didn't notice. Actually, my husband and I were just talking about putting a soundproof mat in the living room.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {ああ、}それはありがたいです。
lines.en: Oh, that would be very kind.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あと、}寝る前は、{なるべく}寝室で遊ばせるようにしますね。寝室なら、田村さんのお部屋の真上じゃないので。
lines.en: And before bed, I'll try to have him play in the bedroom. The bedroom isn't directly above your place.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうですか。いや、そこまでしていただかなくても…
lines.en: Is that so? Oh, you really needn't go that far…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いえいえ、お互い様ですから。{もし、}また気になったら、遠慮なくおっしゃってください。
lines.en: Not at all, we're neighbours. If it bothers you again, please don't hesitate to say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。{いや、}正直、言いに来るの、ちょっと緊張してたんですよ。
lines.en: Thank you. To be honest, I was a bit nervous about coming to say it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ですよね。わざわざありがとうございました。
lines.en: I can imagine. Thank you for taking the trouble.

questions.question: What exactly does Tamura ask for?
choices: More care with noise after ten o'clock
That the noise stop altogether
That they lay a mat in the living room
That the child sleep in another room

questions.question: Which idea had the Matsumotos already been considering before Tamura came?
choices: Having their son play in the bedroom
Putting their son to bed before ten
Soundproofing the living room floor
Asking the neighbours if the noise was a problem

questions.question: How did Tamura feel about coming upstairs?
choices: Irritated after many sleepless nights
Anxious about raising the subject
Sure the family would be defensive
Embarrassed about complaining about a child

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {で、}母さんのことなんだけど。{あの、}また台所で転んだって、近所の人から電話があって。
lines.en: So, about Mum. A neighbour called to say she fell in the kitchen again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、また？ だから言ったじゃん、一人暮らしはもう限界だって。
lines.en: What, again? I told you, living alone has reached its limit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: いや、分かってるよ。{でも、}本人が家を出たくないって言ってるんだから、{その、}無理やり施設ってわけにも…
lines.en: I know. But she says she doesn't want to leave the house, so we can't just force her into a home…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 施設なんて誰も言ってないでしょ。{ただ、}週一で様子見に行くだけじゃ足りないって話。
lines.en: Nobody said a home. I'm saying checking on her once a week isn't enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {そりゃ、}俺だって、できることなら毎日行きたいよ。でも、片道二時間だぞ。
lines.en: Well, I'd go every day if I could. But it's two hours each way.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 分かってる。{だから、}{なんか}、私が近くに住んでるからって、負担が全部こっちに来てる感じがするの。
lines.en: I know. That's why it feels like, just because I live nearby, the whole burden falls on me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あー、}…それは、ごめん。そこまで考えてなかった。
lines.en: Ah… sorry. I hadn't thought about it like that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {で、}提案なんだけど、平日は訪問介護を頼んで、その費用は兄さんが多めに出す、っていうのはどう？
lines.en: So here's my proposal: on weekdays we get a home-care service, and you pay more of the cost. How about that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {うーん、}{お金は、}お金はいいよ、それで。{ただ、}母さん、知らない人を家に入れるの、嫌がるかもな。
lines.en: Hmm, the money's fine by me. But Mum might not like having strangers in the house.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そこは、{まあ、}最初は私も一緒にいるようにするから。
lines.en: I'll make sure I'm there too at first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 分かった。{あと、}週末は、月に二回は俺が行くよ。{その、}泊まりで。
lines.en: OK. And I'll come at least two weekends a month. Staying over.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ほんとに？ {いや、}それ、すごく助かる。
lines.en: Really? That would help so much.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {じゃあ、}今度の日曜、{母さん、}母さんも入れて三人で話そう。
lines.en: Then let's talk it over this Sunday, the three of us, with Mum.

questions.question: What is Yumi's underlying complaint?
choices: Kenichi wants to put their mother in a home
Their mother won't accept any help
Kenichi only visits once a week
The care falls on her because she lives close by

questions.question: What do they agree about the cost of care?
choices: They'll split it evenly
Kenichi will pay the larger share
Their mother will pay from her savings
The money will go towards a care home

questions.question: What will Kenichi do in addition?
choices: Stay with their mother two weekends a month
Visit every weekday after work
Be there when the carers first come
Call the neighbour each week

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {そういえば、}隆さんの会社、完全に出社に戻ったんだって？
lines.en: By the way, I heard your company went fully back to the office?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうなんだよ。四月から週五で。{まあ、}最初は面倒だなって思ってたんだけど。
lines.en: Yeah. Five days a week since April. Well, at first I thought it'd be a pain.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: え、過去形？
lines.en: Wait, past tense?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うん、}{いや、}意外と悪くなくて。{その、}隣の席の人にちょっと聞けば済むことが、在宅だとメールで半日待ちとかだったじゃん。
lines.en: Yeah, it's surprisingly not bad. Things you could sort out by asking the person next to you used to mean half a day waiting on email when we were remote.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あー、}それはあるかも。
lines.en: Ah, that's true.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: でも私は{無理、}絶対無理だな。通勤一時間半だよ？ 往復三時間って、{なんか}人生もったいなくない？
lines.en: But I could never do it. My commute's an hour and a half. Three hours round trip — isn't that a waste of your life?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {まあ、}それは距離によるよね。俺は二十分だから。
lines.en: Well, that depends on distance. Mine's twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: でしょ。それに、うちの部署、{その、}一人で集中する作業が多いから、家のほうがはかどるんだよね。
lines.en: Right. Plus, my department does a lot of work where you concentrate alone, so I get more done at home.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: なるほどね。
lines.en: I see.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ただ、美穂ちゃん、前に、在宅だと{なんか}孤独だって言ってなかった？
lines.en: But Miho, didn't you say before that working from home was lonely?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あ、}それは…{まあ、}言った。だから今は、週一だけオフィスに行くようにしてる。
lines.en: Ah, that… yeah, I said that. So now I make a point of going to the office once a week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ほら、結局そこなんだって。{たぶん}一番いいのは、選べることなんだよ。
lines.en: See, that's the point. What's best is probably being able to choose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {うーん、}悔しいけど、それは同意。
lines.en: Hmm, I hate to say it, but I agree.

questions.question: How has Takashi's attitude to working in the office changed?
choices: He still finds it a nuisance
He likes it more than he expected
He now wants to work from home again
He only minds it because of the commute

questions.question: What has Miho started doing, and why?
choices: Working in cafés to cut her commute
Going into the office weekly because remote work felt lonely
Asking colleagues by email instead of waiting
Moving closer to work to save time

questions.question: What do they finally agree on?
choices: Having the choice matters most
The office suits most people better
Remote work is best for focused tasks
A short commute makes the office worthwhile

speakers.name: 吉田
speakers.hint: tour guide on the phone, flustered, fast

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: もしもし、小川さん？ {あの、}吉田です。ちょっとまずいことになってて。
lines.en: Hello, Ogawa-san? It's Yoshida. Something's gone a bit wrong.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: どうしました？
lines.en: What's happened?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {えっと、}{その、}お寺の見学のあと、自由時間にしたんですけど、集合時間になっても四人戻ってこなくて。
lines.en: Well, after the temple tour I gave them free time, but four people didn't come back by the meeting time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 四人ですか。{えっと、}同じグループの方たちですか？
lines.en: Four? Are they all together?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい、ご夫婦二組で。{携帯、}携帯に電話しても、{なんか}電源が切れてるみたいで…
lines.en: Yes, two couples. And when I call their mobiles, the phones seem to be switched off…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うーん、}もしかして、参道のお土産屋さんのほうに行ってません？ あそこ、裏道が分かりにくくて、よく迷う人がいるんですよ。
lines.en: Hmm, could they have gone to the souvenir shops on the approach road? The back streets there are confusing, and people often get lost.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あ、}そういえば、お昼のとき、甘いもの食べたいって{話して、}言ってました。
lines.en: Oh, come to think of it, at lunch they said they wanted something sweet.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {じゃあ、}たぶんそこですね。吉田さんは、残りのお客様とバスで待っててください。
lines.en: Then that's probably it. You wait on the bus with the rest of the guests.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: でも、次の旅館のチェックインが四時なんですよ。
lines.en: But check-in at the next inn is at four.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: それは僕が旅館に電話して、三十分遅れるって伝えておきます。{で、}僕、今ちょうど近くにいるんで、探しに行きます。
lines.en: I'll call the inn and tell them we'll be thirty minutes late. And I'm nearby right now, so I'll go look for them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: え、いいんですか？ 助かります！ {あ、}四人とも赤い帽子かぶってます。
lines.en: Really? Thank you so much! Oh, all four are wearing red hats.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 了解です。見つかったらすぐ連絡します。{あの、}その間、お客様に事情を説明しといてください。
lines.en: Got it. I'll call as soon as I find them. Meanwhile, please explain the situation to the guests.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 分かりました。{えっと、}本当にすみません。
lines.en: Understood. I'm really sorry.

questions.question: Why does Ogawa think the missing guests are near the souvenir shops?
choices: Their phones showed they were there
They had wanted a sweet snack, and people get lost there
They had been seen there at lunchtime
The temple tour ended right next to them

questions.question: What will happen about the inn?
choices: Yoshida will phone to cancel
Check-in will be moved to four o'clock
The bus will go ahead without the four
Ogawa will warn them the group is running late

questions.question: What is Yoshida's job while Ogawa searches?
choices: Keeping the other guests informed on the bus
Searching the back streets herself
Calling the missing guests again
Phoning the inn about the delay

dialogues.title: A break on the night shift

speakers.name: 遠藤
speakers.hint: experienced nurse, tired but warm, gently teasing

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {はあ、}やっと休憩だね。林くん、夕飯食べた？
lines.en: Phew, finally a break. Hayashi-kun, have you eaten?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {いや、}まだです。{さっき、}三〇五号室のナースコールが続いちゃって。
lines.en: No, not yet. Room 305 kept pressing the call button.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あー、}佐藤さんね。{なんか}夜になると不安になっちゃうみたいで。
lines.en: Ah, Mrs Sato. She seems to get anxious once it's night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうなんですよ。{その、}用事があるっていうより、{たぶん}誰かと話したいだけなんですよね。
lines.en: Exactly. It's less that she needs something and more that she just wants someone to talk to.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うん。
lines.en: Mm.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {でも、}僕、忙しいとつい、そっけない対応しちゃって。ちょっと反省してます。
lines.en: But when I'm busy I end up being curt with her. I feel a bit bad about it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {まあ、}夜勤で全員にゆっくり付き合うのは無理だよ。{ただ、}最初に『何時ごろまた来ますね』って言っとくと、落ち着く人、けっこう多いよ。
lines.en: Well, on nights you can't spend time with everyone. But if you tell them at the start, 'I'll come back around such-and-such a time', a lot of people settle down.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あ、}なるほど。{待つ、}先が見えると待てるってことですね。
lines.en: Ah, I see. If they know when, they can wait.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうそう。{あ、}そういえば、林くん、来月から日勤に戻るんだっけ？
lines.en: Right. Oh, by the way, you're going back to day shifts next month, aren't you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい、一応。でも、正直、夜勤のほうが、{なんか}患者さんとじっくり話せる気がして、ちょっと寂しいです。
lines.en: Yes, supposedly. But honestly, it feels like on nights I can really talk with patients, so I'm a bit sad.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: へえ、意外。{じゃあ、}さっきの佐藤さんのことも、ほんとは気になってたんだ。
lines.en: Oh, that's a surprise. So you really were worried about Mrs Sato earlier.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {まあ、}そうですね。{じゃあ、}食べたら、さっきのやり方、早速試してみます。
lines.en: Well, yes. So after I eat, I'll try what you said right away.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うん。{あ、}これ、差し入れのおにぎり。一個あげる。
lines.en: Good. Oh, here — someone brought rice balls. Have one.

questions.question: What does Hayashi think the patient in room 305 really wants?
choices: Help with something she needs
Someone to keep her company
To be moved to a quieter room
Her medication earlier in the night

questions.question: What does Endo advise?
choices: Spend longer with each patient
Ask another nurse to answer her calls
Say when you will next come by
Visit her before she starts calling

questions.question: How does Hayashi feel about moving to days?
choices: A little sad to lose the time to talk with patients
Relieved to escape the busy nights
Nervous about working with new staff
Glad he'll finally eat on time

speakers.name: 木村
speakers.hint: kind manager, soft, choosing words carefully

speakers.name: 藤井
speakers.hint: junior employee, polite, tense then receptive

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 藤井さん、ちょっといいかな。{あ、}大した話じゃないから、座って。
lines.en: Fujii-san, got a minute? Oh, it's nothing big, have a seat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい。{えっと、}{何か、}何かありましたか？
lines.en: Yes. Um, is something wrong?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}昨日のプレゼン、{その、}資料はすごくよくできてたよ。データの整理も丁寧だったし。
lines.en: No, no. Yesterday's presentation — the materials were really well done. The data was neatly organised, too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。
lines.en: Thank you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {ただ、}{なんていうか、}結論が最後までなかなか出てこなかったかなって。先方の部長、途中で時計見てたの、気づいた？
lines.en: Only, how to put it, the conclusion didn't really come out until the very end. Did you notice their department head checking his watch halfway through?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {あ、}…はい、気づいてました。{その、}焦って、{余計に、}余計に説明が長くなっちゃって。
lines.en: Ah… yes, I noticed. I panicked, and that made my explanation even longer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うんうん。
lines.en: Mm-hm.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: だから、次からは、最初の一分で結論と、お願いしたいことを言っちゃおう。細かいデータは、聞かれたら出せばいいから。
lines.en: So from next time, let's say the conclusion and what we're asking for in the first minute. You can bring out the detailed data if they ask.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: でも、{あの、}根拠を先に見せないと、納得してもらえないかなって…
lines.en: But, um, I thought if I didn't show the evidence first, they wouldn't be convinced…

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: その気持ちは分かる。{ただ、}忙しい人ほど、先に結論が分かったほうが、根拠も落ち着いて聞けるんだよ。
lines.en: I understand that feeling. But the busier people are, the more calmly they can listen to the evidence once they know the conclusion.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: なるほど…確かに、自分が聞く側だったらそうかもしれません。
lines.en: I see… If I were the one listening, that might be true.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {じゃあ、}来週の{会議、}社内会議で、一回練習してみようか。{僕が、}僕が先方の部長役やるから。
lines.en: So, at next week's internal meeting, let's try it once for practice. I'll play their department head.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: え、はい、お願いします。{ちょっと、}緊張しますけど。
lines.en: Oh, yes, please. I'll be a bit nervous, though.

questions.question: What is Kimura's main criticism of the presentation?
choices: The data was badly organised
She spoke too quickly out of nerves
She ran over the time she was given
Her main point came far too late

questions.question: Why had Fujii put the evidence first?
choices: She believed the client wouldn't be persuaded otherwise
Kimura had told her to last time
The client's manager had asked for data
She wanted to fill the time available

questions.question: What is planned for next week?
choices: Fujii will present to the client again
A rehearsal with Kimura playing the client
Kimura will give the presentation himself
Fujii will send the data to the client in advance

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {ねえ、}今朝のニュース見た？ 大手の銀行が、{その、}事務作業の三割を人工知能に任せるって。
lines.en: Hey, did you see the news this morning? A major bank is handing thirty percent of its office work to AI.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 見た見た。{で、}人員を五年で二千人減らすって話でしょ。
lines.en: Yeah, I saw. And they'll cut two thousand staff over five years, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうそう。{いや、}正直ちょっと怖くなった。俺の仕事も、データの入力とかチェックばっかりだし。
lines.en: Exactly. Honestly, it scared me a bit. My job's all data entry and checking too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {うーん、}でもさ、記事、最後まで読んだ？
lines.en: Hmm, but did you read the article to the end?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {いや、}見出しだけ…
lines.en: No, just the headline…

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: やっぱり。{あの、}減らすって言っても、ほとんどは定年で自然に辞める分で、{その、}残った人は窓口とかに移るらしいよ。
lines.en: Thought so. Even though they say cuts, most of it's people retiring naturally, and the rest will apparently move to things like the customer counters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: へえ、そうなんだ。{じゃあ、}クビになるわけじゃないんだ。
lines.en: Huh, really. So nobody's getting fired.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {まあ、}今回はね。{ただ、}{仕事の、}仕事の中身は確実に変わるよね。
lines.en: Well, this time. But what the work involves is definitely going to change.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {なんか}それって、結局、人間にしかできないことをやれってことでしょ？ それが何なのか、いまいち分かんないんだよね。
lines.en: Isn't that basically saying do what only humans can do? I don't really get what that is.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: {えっと、}例えば、お客さんの話をちゃんと聞くとか、{その、}判断に責任を持つとか？
lines.en: Um, like really listening to customers, or taking responsibility for decisions?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: {あー、}なるほどね。{じゃあ、}俺も、前から気になってた資格の勉強、{その、}始めてみようかな。
lines.en: Ah, I see. Then maybe I'll start studying for that qualification I've been curious about.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いいじゃん。でも、まずはニュースを最後まで読むとこからね。
lines.en: Good idea. But first, start by reading the news to the end.

questions.question: What had Sho misunderstood about the news?
choices: He thought the bank was closing branches
He thought the job cuts meant people being fired
He thought his own company was involved
He thought the change would happen this year

questions.question: According to Emi, what kind of work will remain for people?
choices: Checking the data the system produces
Training the new software
Listening to customers and owning decisions
Handling data entry that machines get wrong

questions.question: What does Emi's last remark suggest?
choices: Sho should read properly before worrying
Sho should give up on the qualification
Sho should find a job at a bank
Sho should stop following the news

dialogues.title: Getting ready for a client visit

speakers.name: 山口
speakers.hint: attentive, polite, a little flustered at the mistake

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 山口さん、明日の午後、取引先の皆様がいらっしゃるので、準備をお願いしたいんだけど。
lines.en: Yamaguchi, our clients are coming tomorrow afternoon, so I'd like you to handle the preparations.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい。会議室の予約はもう済ませてあります。
lines.en: Yes. I've already booked the meeting room.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ありがとう。それから、先方に提出する資料なんだけど、売上のデータが先月のままになっていたよ。
lines.en: Thanks. Also, the materials we're giving them still have last month's sales data.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 申し訳ありません。すぐに最新の数字に差し替えます。
lines.en: I'm very sorry. I'll replace them with the latest figures right away.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うん、それを最優先で頼む。印刷は明日の朝でも間に合うから。
lines.en: Yes, make that your top priority. The printing can wait until tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 承知しました。お茶菓子の手配はどうしましょうか。
lines.en: Understood. What should I do about the tea and snacks?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それは総務の佐々木さんに頼んであるから、心配しなくていいよ。
lines.en: I've already asked Sasaki in general affairs, so don't worry about that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。あと、駅までのお迎えは必要でしょうか。
lines.en: All right. And will someone need to meet them at the station?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 先方は車でいらっしゃるそうだから、駐車場の確保だけしておいてくれる？
lines.en: They're coming by car, apparently, so could you just make sure there's parking for them?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい。では、資料の修正が終わりましたら、一度ご確認いただけますか。
lines.en: Yes. Then once I've fixed the materials, could you check them over?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: もちろん。夕方までに送ってくれれば目を通しておくよ。
lines.en: Of course. If you send them by early evening, I'll look through them.

questions.question: What will Yamaguchi do first?
choices: Book the meeting room for the visit
Print the materials for the clients

Secure parking spaces for the clients

Preparing the refreshments
Printing the materials
Meeting the clients at the station
