The visit has been moved to the morning
The section chief will greet them himself
The visitors will be driving over

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 中村さん、卒業論文の計画書、読ませてもらいました。
lines.en: Nakamura, I've read your graduation thesis plan.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。いかがでしたでしょうか。
lines.en: Thank you. What did you think?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: テーマ自体は興味深いんだけど、少し範囲が広すぎるかな。
lines.en: The theme itself is interesting, but the scope is a bit too broad, I think.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 地方の人口と観光の関係、という点でしょうか。
lines.en: You mean the relationship between regional population and tourism?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そう。全国を対象にすると、一年ではとても調査しきれないと思うよ。
lines.en: Right. If you cover the whole country, I don't think you can possibly finish the research in a year.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: では、地域を一つに絞ったほうがよろしいでしょうか。
lines.en: Then would it be better to narrow it down to one region?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うん、例えば君の出身地のように、実際に現地で話を聞ける所がいいね。
lines.en: Yes. Somewhere like your hometown, where you can actually talk to people on site, would be good.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: なるほど。アンケートも予定していたのですが、それはどうでしょう。
lines.en: I see. I was also planning a questionnaire. What about that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 悪くはないけど、どれだけ回答が集まるかを考えると、インタビュー中心のほうが現実的だろうね。
lines.en: It's not bad, but considering how many responses you'd actually get, focusing on interviews is probably more realistic.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。これまでの研究の整理は、あれで足りていますか。
lines.en: Understood. Is my review of earlier research sufficient as it is?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そこはよく調べてあった。来週までに修正した計画書を出してください。
lines.en: That part was well researched. Please hand in a revised plan by next week.

questions.question: What does the professor see as the main weakness of the plan?
choices: It tries to cover too much for a one-year project
The topic itself is not interesting enough
The review of earlier research is too thin
The questionnaire has too few questions

questions.question: How does the professor suggest she gather her data?
choices: Mainly through a nationwide questionnaire
By talking to people in a single region she can visit
Only by reviewing earlier studies
Through a questionnaire sent to her hometown

questions.question: What will the student do next?
choices: Start interviews in her hometown this week
Send out the questionnaire right away
Add more earlier research to the plan
Hand in a revised plan within a week

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 今日は、町で小さなビール工房を営んでいらっしゃる森さんにお越しいただきました。
lines.en: Today we're joined by Mr. Mori, who runs a small beer workshop here in town.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: よろしくお願いします。
lines.en: Nice to be here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: もともとは会社員だったそうですね。
lines.en: I hear you were originally an office worker.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ええ、十年ほど営業の仕事をしていました。趣味で始めたビール造りに、すっかりはまってしまいまして。
lines.en: Yes, I worked in sales for about ten years. Then I got completely hooked on brewing, which I'd started as a hobby.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 会社を辞めることに、不安はありませんでしたか。
lines.en: Weren't you anxious about quitting your company?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: もちろんありました。ただ、地元の農家さんが育てた麦を使えば、ここにしかない味が作れると思ったんです。
lines.en: Of course I was. But I thought that with barley grown by local farmers, I could make a flavor you can't find anywhere else.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: なるほど。原料にこだわっていらっしゃるんですね。
lines.en: I see. So you're particular about your ingredients.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい。そのぶん値段は大手の商品より高くなりますが、お客さんには産地の話も一緒に楽しんでほしいので。
lines.en: Yes. That makes it pricier than the big brands, but I want customers to enjoy the story of where it comes from as well.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 今後の目標を教えてください。
lines.en: Tell us about your goals for the future.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 規模を広げるより、今の品質を守りたいですね。来年は、工房の隣に小さな飲食スペースを作る予定です。
lines.en: Rather than growing bigger, I want to protect the quality we have now. Next year I plan to open a small food and drink space next to the workshop.

questions.question: What made Mori decide to go into brewing full-time?
choices: He had grown tired of working in sales
A local farmer asked him to use his barley
He saw a chance to make a flavor unique to the area
He wanted to sell beer more cheaply than big brands

questions.question: What are Mori's plans for next year?
choices: Increase production to supply larger stores
Add a small place to eat and drink by the workshop
Cut his prices to compete with major brands
Hand the workshop over to a local farmer

dialogues.title: Booking a hotel for a company group

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: お電話ありがとうございます。ホテル青葉、予約係でございます。
lines.en: Thank you for calling Hotel Aoba reservations.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 来月の十五日に、三十名ほどの団体で宿泊をお願いしたいのですが。
lines.en: I'd like to book a stay for a group of about thirty on the fifteenth of next month.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: かしこまりました。十五日ですと、あいにく和室は満室でございまして、洋室でしたらご用意できます。
lines.en: Certainly. On the fifteenth, unfortunately, the Japanese-style rooms are fully booked, but we can offer Western-style rooms.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 洋室ですか。実は会社の研修旅行なので、できれば宴会場も使いたいんですが。
lines.en: Western-style, huh. Actually it's a company training trip, so if possible we'd like to use a banquet hall too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 宴会場は空いております。二十名様以上ですと、団体割引で一割お安くなります。
lines.en: The banquet hall is available. For groups of twenty or more, there's a ten percent group discount.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: それはありがたいです。もう少し安くなりませんか。予算が厳しくて。
lines.en: That's helpful. Can't you go a little lower? Our budget is tight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 申し訳ございません、料金はこれ以上は…。ただ、夕食のコースを一つ下げていただければ、お一人様千円ほど抑えられますが。
lines.en: I'm sorry, the rate itself can't go any lower... However, if you choose the next dinner course down, you could save about a thousand yen per person.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: なるほど。では、その案で検討させてください。キャンセル料はいつからかかりますか。
lines.en: I see. Let me consider it on that basis, then. From when do cancellation fees apply?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 七日前からでございます。人数の変更は三日前まで承ります。
lines.en: From seven days before. Changes to the number of guests are accepted up to three days before.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。社内で確認して、明日までにお返事します。
lines.en: Understood. I'll check within the company and get back to you by tomorrow.

questions.question: How could Ishii bring the cost down further?
choices: By switching to Japanese-style rooms
By choosing a less expensive dinner
By bringing ten more people
By not using the banquet hall

questions.question: Which statement matches what the hotel explained?
choices: The group can change its numbers until three days before
Cancellation fees start three days before the stay
Groups of thirty or more get twenty percent off
Japanese-style rooms can be added for a small fee

questions.question: What will Ishii do next?
choices: Confirm the booking on the spot
Look for a hotel with Japanese-style rooms
Change the number of guests to twenty
Consult his company before replying

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 松本さん、昨日の面接の二人、どう思いました？
lines.en: Matsumoto, what did you think of the two people we interviewed yesterday?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうですね。経験で言えば、断然、一人目の田村さんですよね。
lines.en: Well, in terms of experience, the first one, Tamura, is far ahead.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 確かに。前の会社で営業を八年ですから、即戦力にはなると思います。
lines.en: True. Eight years in sales at his last company, so he could contribute from day one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ただ、少し自分のやり方へのこだわりが強い印象を受けました。
lines.en: But I got the impression he's rather attached to doing things his own way.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ああ、それは私も感じました。うちのチームは協調性が大事ですからね。
lines.en: Oh, I felt that too. Cooperation is important on our team.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 二人目の岡田さんは経験は浅いですけど、質問への答え方が柔軟でしたね。
lines.en: The second one, Okada, doesn't have much experience, but he answered questions flexibly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ええ。ただ、一から教えるとなると、一人前に育てるには時間がかかりますよ。
lines.en: Yes. But if we teach him from scratch, it'll take time to bring him up to speed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 来年の春に大きなプロジェクトが始まることを考えると、それまでに間に合うかどうか…。
lines.en: Considering the big project starting next spring, I wonder whether he'd be ready in time...

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうなんですよ。でも、長い目で見れば、岡田さんのほうがチームに合う気がします。
lines.en: Exactly. But in the long run, I feel Okada would fit the team better.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: じゃあ、岡田さんを推して、春までの研修計画も一緒に部長に提案しましょうか。
lines.en: Then shall we recommend Okada and propose a training plan up to spring to the department head along with it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それがいいですね。
lines.en: That sounds good.

questions.question: Whom do they decide to recommend, and why?
choices: Tamura, because he could contribute at once
Tamura, because of his long sales career
Okada, because he seems adaptable and a good fit
Okada, because he has more sales experience

questions.question: What worries them about choosing Okada?
choices: He is too attached to his own methods
He may not be trained in time for the spring project
He answered their questions too cautiously
He cannot start work until next spring

dialogues.title: Lease renewal and a rent increase

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 小林さん、来月で契約の更新になりますが、どうされますか。
lines.en: Ms. Kobayashi, your lease is up for renewal next month. What would you like to do?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい、引き続き住みたいと思っています。
lines.en: I'd like to keep living here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それはよかった。ただ、実は次の契約から家賃を五千円上げさせていただきたいんです。
lines.en: Good to hear. The thing is, from the next contract I'd like to raise the rent by five thousand yen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 五千円ですか…。正直、ちょっと厳しいですね。
lines.en: Five thousand... Honestly, that's a bit hard for me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 周りの相場も上がっていますし、税金も上がりましてね。
lines.en: Rents around here have gone up, and so have my taxes, you see.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 事情はわかるんですが…。この部屋に住んで六年、一度も家賃を滞納したことはありませんし、エアコンも古いままなので…。
lines.en: I understand your situation, but... I've lived here six years without once paying late, and the air conditioner is still the old one...

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ああ、エアコンね。確かに、あれはもう寿命ですね。
lines.en: Ah, the air conditioner. It's true, that one's at the end of its life.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 例えば、エアコンを新しくしていただけるなら、値上げも考えさせていただきたいんですが。
lines.en: If, say, you could replace the air conditioner, I'd be willing to consider the increase.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: なるほど。では、エアコンは交換して、値上げは三千円ということでどうでしょう。
lines.en: I see. Then how about I replace the air conditioner and make the increase three thousand yen?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: それなら、納得です。ありがとうございます。
lines.en: That I can accept. Thank you.

questions.question: What do they finally agree on?
choices: A 5,000-yen increase and a new air conditioner
No increase, given her record of paying on time
A 3,000-yen increase with the old air conditioner
A smaller increase and a new air conditioner

questions.question: How does Kobayashi argue against the original increase?
choices: She says rents nearby have actually fallen
She points to her reliable payments and the aging air conditioner
She says she cannot afford any increase at all
She says the tax rise is not her responsibility

speakers.name: 大野
speakers.hint: polite, a little unsure of the procedures

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 次の方、どうぞ。本日はどのようなご用件でしょうか。
lines.en: Next, please. How can I help you today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 保育園の費用の補助について伺いたいんですが。
lines.en: I'd like to ask about subsidies for daycare costs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: かしこまりました。お子様は何歳でいらっしゃいますか。
lines.en: Certainly. How old is your child?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 二歳です。今は妻が育児休業中で、来年の四月から預けたいと考えています。
lines.en: Two. My wife is on childcare leave now, and we're thinking of putting our child in daycare from next April.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 三歳未満のお子様の場合は、世帯の所得によって補助の金額が変わります。
lines.en: For children under three, the subsidy amount depends on household income.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうなんですか。申請には何が必要でしょうか。
lines.en: Is that so. What do I need to apply?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 申請書と、ご夫婦お二人分の所得を証明する書類が必要です。
lines.en: The application form, plus documents proving the income of both of you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 妻の分は勤め先から取り寄せないといけませんね。締め切りはいつですか。
lines.en: I'll have to get my wife's from her employer, then. When's the deadline?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 四月入園の場合、十一月末が締め切りです。ただ、書類がそろわない場合でも、先に申請書だけ出していただくことはできます。
lines.en: For April entry, the deadline is the end of November. But even if you don't have all the documents yet, you can submit just the application form first.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: では、とりあえず今日は申請書だけ出して帰ります。
lines.en: In that case, I'll just hand in the application form today for now.

questions.question: What does the father decide to do today?
choices: Hand in every document, including proof of income
Get his wife's income papers from her workplace
Turn in only the form and bring the rest later
Enroll his child in daycare for next April

questions.question: What determines how much subsidy the family receives?
choices: How much the household earns
How long the wife's leave lasts
Which month the child starts daycare
Whether both parents submit forms together

speakers.name: 西田
speakers.hint: slow, a little set in his ways

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 西田さん、今日から新しいお薬が一つ追加になっています。
lines.en: Mr. Nishida, one new medicine has been added starting today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ああ、血圧の薬ですね。先生から聞いています。
lines.en: Ah, the blood pressure one. The doctor told me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい。一日一回、朝食の後に飲んでください。
lines.en: Yes. Please take it once a day, after breakfast.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 前の薬は夜に飲んでいるんですが、一緒に夜じゃだめですか。
lines.en: I take my other medicine at night. Can't I take them together at night?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: この薬は、飲み始めにめまいが出ることがあるので、夜ですと、夜中にお手洗いに行く時にふらついて危ないんです。
lines.en: This medicine can cause dizziness when you first start it, so if you take it at night, you might be unsteady going to the bathroom in the middle of the night, which is dangerous.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: なるほど。ほかに気をつけることはありますか。
lines.en: I see. Is there anything else I should be careful about?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: グレープフルーツは薬の効き目を強めてしまうので、控えてください。
lines.en: Grapefruit makes the medicine act more strongly, so please avoid it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 毎朝ジュースで飲んでいるんですが…。
lines.en: But I drink it as juice every morning...

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: では、ジュースはほかの果物のものに変えていただけますか。それから、足のむくみが続くようでしたら、ご連絡ください。
lines.en: Then could you switch to juice made from other fruit? Also, if swelling in your legs continues, please contact us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。むくみが出たら、すぐに薬をやめたほうがいいですか。
lines.en: All right. If I get swelling, should I stop the medicine right away?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 二、三日で治まれば心配いりません。続くようなら、ご自分の判断でやめずに、まずご相談ください。
lines.en: If it settles in two or three days, there's nothing to worry about. If it continues, don't stop on your own; please consult us first.

questions.question: Why should he take the new medicine in the morning?
choices: It must be taken on a full stomach
Dizziness at night could make him fall
It interferes with his evening medicine
The doctor wants it taken with juice

questions.question: What will he change about his mornings?
choices: He will take both medicines then
He will stop drinking juice entirely
He will drink a different kind of juice
He will eat grapefruit only at night

questions.question: What should he do if the swelling does not go away?
choices: Stop the medicine at once
Start taking it at night instead
Wait another few days and see
Talk to the pharmacy before changing anything

dialogues.title: Planning a festival on a smaller budget

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 吉田さん、夏祭りの件なんだが、市からの補助金が去年の半分になってしまってね。
lines.en: Yoshida, about the summer festival: the city's subsidy has been cut to half of last year's.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 半分ですか。それは痛いですね。
lines.en: Half? That hurts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そこで、何を削るか相談したいんだ。
lines.en: So I want to talk about what to cut.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 一番費用がかかっているのは、最後の花火ですよね。
lines.en: The most expensive thing is the fireworks at the end, isn't it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うん。でも、花火は毎年楽しみにしている人が多いから、できれば残したい。
lines.en: Yes. But lots of people look forward to the fireworks every year, so I'd like to keep them if we can.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: では、舞台のゲストを見直すのはどうでしょう。去年はプロの歌手を二人呼びましたが、地元の高校の吹奏楽部に出てもらえば、出演料はほとんどかかりません。
lines.en: Then how about rethinking the stage guests? Last year we brought in two professional singers, but if the local high school band performs, there's almost no appearance fee.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それはいい考えだね。地域とのつながりも深まるし。
lines.en: That's a good idea. It would strengthen ties with the community, too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: あとは、商店街の各店舗に協力金をお願いする方法もありますが…。
lines.en: There's also the option of asking each shop in the arcade for a contribution...

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 今年は景気がよくないから、お店に負担をかけるのは避けたいな。
lines.en: Business is bad this year, so I'd rather not put a burden on the shops.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。では、さっそく高校に問い合わせてみます。
lines.en: Understood. Then I'll get in touch with the high school right away.

questions.question: What do they decide to cut back on?
choices: The fireworks at the end of the night
Paid professional acts on the stage
Contributions from local shops
The high school band's performance

questions.question: Why does the chairman not want to ask the shops for money?
choices: The shops are struggling this year
The city subsidy will cover the gap
The fireworks matter more to residents
The high school band costs almost nothing

questions.question: What will Yoshida do next?
choices: Cancel the professional singers
Visit each shop in the arcade
Ask the city for a larger subsidy
Contact the local high school

speakers.name: 林
speakers.hint: efficient office manager, a little pressed for time

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: もしもし、先日オフィス家具を注文した林ですが、配達の日を変更していただきたいんです。
lines.en: Hello, this is Hayashi. I ordered office furniture the other day, and I'd like to change the delivery date.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 林様ですね。ご注文を確認いたします。机が十台と椅子が十脚、今週の金曜日の配達でございますね。
lines.en: Ms. Hayashi, let me check your order. Ten desks and ten chairs, for delivery this Friday, correct?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい。実は、その日にビルの工事が入ることになりまして。
lines.en: Yes. It turns out there's going to be construction work in the building that day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: かしこまりました。最短ですと来週の火曜日になりますが。
lines.en: Certainly. The earliest we can do is next Tuesday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 火曜日は午前中でしたら大丈夫です。
lines.en: Tuesday is fine if it's in the morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 申し訳ございません。火曜日は午後の便しか空いておりません。午前中をご希望でしたら、木曜日になります。
lines.en: I'm very sorry, on Tuesday only the afternoon slot is free. If you'd prefer a morning, it would be Thursday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 木曜ですか…。水曜から新しい社員が来るので、できればその前に…。
lines.en: Thursday... New employees start on Wednesday, so if possible, before that...

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: でしたら、火曜日の午後になります。ただ、組み立ての作業が夕方までかかる可能性がございます。
lines.en: In that case, Tuesday afternoon. However, the assembly work may run into the evening.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それでも構いません。火曜の午後でお願いします。
lines.en: That's fine. Tuesday afternoon, please.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: かしこまりました。搬入の際は必ずどなたかにお立ち会いいただく必要がございます。それから、エレベーターの使用許可をビルの管理会社から取っておいていただけますか。
lines.en: Certainly. Someone must be present when the items are brought in. Also, could you get permission to use the elevator from the building management company?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: わかりました。管理会社にはこちらから連絡しておきます。
lines.en: Understood. I'll contact the management company myself.

questions.question: When will the furniture be delivered?
choices: This Friday as first planned
Next Tuesday morning
Next Tuesday afternoon
Next Thursday morning

questions.question: Why does Hayashi turn down Thursday?
choices: The building has construction work that day
She wants the furniture before new staff arrive
No one can be present on Thursday
Only an afternoon slot is free on Thursday

questions.question: What does Hayashi need to arrange before the delivery?
choices: Permission to use the building's elevator
A time to assemble the desks herself
A postponement of the construction work
A second call to confirm the time slot

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: こちらが北海道五日間のツアーのお見積もりでございます。
lines.en: Here is the quote for the five-day Hokkaido tour.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。実は、仕事の都合で日程が変わるかもしれなくて、キャンセルの規定を伺いたいんですが。
lines.en: Thank you. Actually, my dates might change because of work, so I'd like to ask about the cancellation rules.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: かしこまりました。出発の二十日前までは無料でございます。それ以降は旅行代金の二十パーセント、前日ですと四十パーセントかかります。
lines.en: Certainly. Up to twenty days before departure it's free. After that it's twenty percent of the tour price, and the day before, forty percent.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 当日だと？
lines.en: And on the day itself?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 当日は五十パーセント、ご連絡なく参加されなかった場合は全額となります。
lines.en: Fifty percent on the day, and the full amount if you don't show up without contacting us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 結構かかりますね。
lines.en: That adds up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ご心配でしたら、こちらの自由度の高いプランもございます。料金は一万円ほど高くなりますが、出発の三日前まで無料で日程を変更できます。
lines.en: If you're concerned, we also have this more flexible plan. It costs about ten thousand yen more, but you can change your dates free of charge up to three days before departure.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 変更だけですか。キャンセルは？
lines.en: Only changes? What about cancelling?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: キャンセルの場合は、通常のプランと同じ扱いになります。
lines.en: Cancellations are treated the same as with the regular plan.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: うーん、行けなくなるというより、日にちがずれる可能性のほうが高いので、そちらのほうが安心ですね。そちらでお願いします。
lines.en: Hmm, it's more likely my dates will shift than that I won't be able to go at all, so that one's safer. I'll take that plan.

questions.question: How much would Okamoto pay if he cancelled the day before departure?
choices: Twenty percent of the price
Forty percent of the price
Half of the price
The whole price

questions.question: Which plan does Okamoto choose, and why?
choices: The regular plan, since it is ten thousand yen cheaper
The regular plan, since cancelling is free until twenty days out
The flexible plan, since it lets him cancel free until three days out
The flexible plan, since his trip is more likely to move than be called off

dialogues.title: Handling a mistake with a client

speakers.name: 前田
speakers.hint: calm senior colleague, supportive but serious

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 川口さん、ちょっといい？さっき、丸山商事の担当の方から電話があったんだけど。
lines.en: Kawaguchi, got a minute? The person in charge at Maruyama Trading called a moment ago.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい…もしかして、昨日お送りした見積書のことでしょうか。
lines.en: Yes... Is it about the estimate I sent yesterday, by any chance?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: うん。金額の桁が一つ違っていたらしいんだ。
lines.en: Yes. Apparently the amount was off by a digit.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: えっ、本当ですか。申し訳ありません。すぐに訂正したものをメールで送ります。
lines.en: What, really? I'm so sorry. I'll email a corrected version right away.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 待って。メールだけで済ませるのはよくないと思うよ。先方はかなりご立腹だったから。
lines.en: Wait. I don't think an email alone will do. They sounded quite upset.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: では、どうすれば…。
lines.en: Then what should I...

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 電話で直接お詫びして、それから訂正したものを持って、午後にでも伺ったほうがいい。
lines.en: Apologize directly by phone, then take the corrected version and visit them, this afternoon if possible.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。課長にも報告したほうがいいですよね。
lines.en: Understood. I should report it to the section chief as well, shouldn't I?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: もちろん。むしろ、それを一番にしないと。後でほかの人から耳に入るほうがまずいから。
lines.en: Of course. In fact, that has to come first. It's worse if he hears about it from someone else later.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい。すぐに課長のところへ行ってきます。
lines.en: Right. I'll go see the section chief now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それと、今後は送る前に、誰かにもう一度確認してもらう習慣をつけるといいよ。
lines.en: And from now on, make a habit of having someone check things again before you send them.

questions.question: What will Kawaguchi do first?
choices: Call the client to apologize
Tell the section chief what happened
Email a corrected estimate
Visit the client with the new estimate

questions.question: Why does Maeda think an email alone is not enough?
choices: The client asked her to come in person
The chief must approve the new estimate first
The client was clearly angry about the error
The corrected figures still need checking

questions.question: What does Maeda advise her to do from now on?
choices: Have a colleague double-check before sending
Always deliver estimates in person
Report every estimate to the section chief
Send estimates by post instead of email

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 在宅勤務で生産性が上がったという調査結果は多いですが、私は一概には言えないと考えています。
lines.en: There are many surveys saying working from home raised productivity, but I don't think it can be stated so simply.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: と、おっしゃいますと？
lines.en: Meaning?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 個人で完結する作業は確かに効率が上がる。しかし、偶然の会話から生まれる発想というものは、数字に表れにくいんです。
lines.en: Tasks one completes alone certainly become more efficient. But the ideas that come out of chance conversations are hard to capture in numbers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: おっしゃることは理解できます。ただ、わが社では通勤がなくなった分、社員の満足度が目に見えて上がりまして、辞める人も減りました。
lines.en: I understand your point. But at our company, with commuting gone, staff satisfaction rose visibly, and fewer people have quit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それ自体は歓迎すべきことです。問題は、それが長期的に見て、新人の育成にどう響くかです。
lines.en: That in itself is welcome. The question is how it affects the development of new hires in the long term.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そこは痛いところを突かれました。実際、入社一、二年目の社員からは、誰に何を聞けばいいのかわからない、という声も上がっています。
lines.en: You've hit a sore spot there. In fact, employees in their first year or two have said they don't know whom to ask about what.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: でしょう。ですから私は、完全在宅か完全出社かという二者択一ではなく、目的に応じて使い分けるべきだと思うんです。
lines.en: Precisely. That's why I think, rather than an either-or choice between fully remote and fully in the office, we should use each according to the purpose.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: その点では意見が一致しますね。私どもも、週二日は全員が顔を合わせる日を設けることを検討しております。
lines.en: On that we agree. We're also considering setting two days a week when everyone meets face to face.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 大事なのは日数という形式ではなく、何のために集まるのかを共有することでしょうね。
lines.en: What matters is not the formality of how many days, but sharing an understanding of why you're gathering.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: おっしゃるとおりです。出社すること自体が目的になってしまっては、本末転倒ですから。
lines.en: Exactly. If coming into the office becomes the goal in itself, that's putting the cart before the horse.

questions.question: What is Fujii's overall view of remote work?
choices: It clearly raises productivity for every kind of work
Staff should return to the office full-time
Its value depends on the task, so both should be combined
It only causes problems for newly hired staff

questions.question: What weakness does Miura concede about her company?
choices: Staff satisfaction has begun to decline
Newer employees struggle to find guidance
More employees have been leaving the company
Productivity figures have not improved

questions.question: What does Miura mean at the end?
choices: Coming in must serve a purpose, not become the purpose
Two office days a week is the ideal number
Remote work has now gone too far
Rules on attendance matter more than goals

dialogues.title: A novelist on writing from many viewpoints

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 新作では、一つの事件を五人の登場人物の視点から描いていらっしゃいますね。
lines.en: In your new novel, you depict a single incident from the viewpoints of five characters.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ええ。同じ出来事でも、立場が違えば見え方がまるで違う。それを読者に体験してほしかったんです。
lines.en: Yes. Even the same event looks entirely different depending on where you stand. I wanted readers to experience that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 執筆の際、最も苦労された点は何でしょう。
lines.en: What was the hardest part of writing it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 語り手ごとに文体を変えることですね。十代の少女と年老いた元刑事が、同じ語彙で語るはずがありませんから。
lines.en: Changing the style for each narrator. A teenage girl and an aging former detective would never speak with the same vocabulary.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 読者の中には、結局誰が真実を語っているのかわからない、という声もあるようですが。
lines.en: Some readers say that in the end they couldn't tell who was telling the truth.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: それは、ある意味で狙いどおりなんです。答えを一つに決めてしまうと、読者が考える余地がなくなってしまう。
lines.en: In a sense, that's exactly what I was aiming for. If I settled on one answer, there'd be no room left for readers to think.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: あえて結末をぼかした、と。
lines.en: So you deliberately blurred the ending.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ぼかしたというより、委ねたと言ってほしいですね。作者の手を離れた時点で、物語は読者のものですから。
lines.en: I'd rather you said I entrusted it. Once a story leaves the author's hands, it belongs to the readers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 次回作も、同じ手法をお考えですか。
lines.en: Are you planning to use the same technique in your next work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: いえ、二番煎じになるのは避けたいので、次は一人の視点に徹して書くつもりです。
lines.en: No. I want to avoid rehashing myself, so next time I intend to write strictly from a single viewpoint.

questions.question: Why did the novelist leave it unclear who was telling the truth?
choices: He himself never decided which narrator was honest
He wanted to leave interpretation open to readers
The five narrators' styles could not be reconciled
Readers had asked him for an open ending

questions.question: What did he find most difficult while writing?
choices: Giving each narrator a distinct voice
Researching how detectives actually work
Deciding how the incident should end
Keeping the timeline of events consistent

questions.question: What does he say about his next book?
choices: It will again use five narrators
It will continue the same incident
It will have a clearly stated ending
It will keep to one character's perspective

dialogues.title: A resident questions a redevelopment plan

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 本日は、駅前の再開発計画について、住民の皆様のご意見を伺いたく参りました。
lines.en: I've come today to hear residents' opinions on the station-front redevelopment plan.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 率直に申し上げて、あの商店街を取り壊して高層マンションを建てるというのは、町の顔をなくすようなものだと思います。
lines.en: To be frank, tearing down that shopping street to build high-rise condos is like erasing the face of the town.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: お気持ちはよくわかります。ただ、商店街の空き店舗は三割を超えており、このままでは衰退の一途をたどるのは目に見えております。
lines.en: I understand how you feel. But over thirty percent of the shops are vacant, and it's plain that, as things stand, it will only keep declining.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 空き店舗が増えたのは、市が長年、手をこまぬいてきた結果ではありませんか。
lines.en: Isn't the rise in empty shops the result of the city sitting on its hands for years?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 耳の痛いご指摘です。反省すべき点は多々あると認識しております。
lines.en: That criticism stings. I recognize there is much we should reflect on.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 再開発そのものに反対しているわけではないんです。ただ、住民の声が計画に反映されていないように感じられて。
lines.en: It's not that I oppose redevelopment itself. I just feel residents' voices aren't reflected in the plan.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そこで、低層階に既存の店舗が優先的に入居できる区画を設ける案を、計画に盛り込むことを検討しております。
lines.en: That's why we're considering adding to the plan an option for sections on the lower floors where existing shops can move in with priority.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 家賃が今の何倍にもなるなら、絵に描いた餅ですよ。
lines.en: If the rent there is several times what they pay now, that's pie in the sky.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: おっしゃるとおりです。家賃の補助についても、来月の説明会までに具体的な案をお示しします。
lines.en: You're quite right. We'll present a concrete proposal on rent support by next month's briefing session as well.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: では、その説明会で改めて判断させていただきます。
lines.en: Then I'll make up my mind again at that session.

questions.question: What is the resident's position on the plan?
choices: She opposes any change to the shopping street
She accepts it if the towers are made lower
She is open to it if residents have a real say
She wants the city to buy up the empty shops

questions.question: What is she implying with her remark about rent?
choices: The drawings of the plan look unrealistic
Priority spaces mean little if shops cannot afford them
The city has made similar promises in the past
The vacant shops will never be filled again

questions.question: What will the councillor bring to next month's session?
choices: A revised design without high-rise condos
Survey results from local residents
A list of shops that will move in
A specific plan for helping with rents

dialogues.title: How far can we trust a study?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 先日、朝食を抜くと成績が下がるという研究が話題になりましたが、先生はあの結果をどうご覧になりますか。
lines.en: Recently a study saying that skipping breakfast lowers grades got a lot of attention. How do you view those results?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 興味深い結果ではありますが、あれをもって因果関係があるとまでは言えないでしょうね。
lines.en: They're interesting results, but on that basis alone you can't go so far as to claim cause and effect.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: と言いますと？
lines.en: What do you mean?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 朝食をとる子どもの家庭は、そもそも生活習慣が整っている傾向にある。成績を左右しているのは、朝食そのものではなく、家庭の環境かもしれないわけです。
lines.en: Families whose children eat breakfast tend to have orderly routines to begin with. What's influencing grades may be the home environment, not breakfast itself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: なるほど。ただ、対象者は二千人と、かなり多かったようですが。
lines.en: I see. But the sample was quite large, two thousand people.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 数が多ければ信頼できるというのは、よくある誤解です。偏った集団をいくら集めても、偏りは消えません。
lines.en: That big numbers make a study reliable is a common misconception. However many people you gather from a skewed group, the skew doesn't disappear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: では、報道する側としては、どう伝えるべきなのでしょう。
lines.en: Then how should we in the media report it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 関連があることと原因であることを混同しないことです。見出しで断定してしまうと、読者はそれを事実として受け止めてしまいますから。
lines.en: Don't confuse being related with being the cause. If a headline states it as certain, readers will take it as fact.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 耳が痛いですね。うちの記事も、まさにそういう見出しでした。
lines.en: That hits home. Our article had exactly that kind of headline.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 責めているわけではありません。ただ、一つの研究で結論を急がず、追試の結果を待つ姿勢が大切だと思います。
lines.en: I'm not blaming you. I just think it's important not to rush to conclusions from one study, and to wait for replications.

questions.question: What is the researcher's main criticism of the study's conclusion?
choices: The link may come from family background rather than breakfast
Two thousand participants were too few to be reliable
Breakfast was shown to have no effect on grades
The researchers had manipulated their data

questions.question: What does the researcher say about the large number of participants?
choices: It makes the findings fairly trustworthy
It proves breakfast is related to grades
It cannot correct a biased sample
It should have been ten times larger

questions.question: Why does the journalist say the comment hits home?
choices: The researcher criticized her by name
She herself often skips breakfast
She had helped design the original study
Her paper had presented the finding as certain

speakers.name: 学芸員
speakers.hint: museum curator, highly deferential keigo, tactful

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 桐生様、このたびはご寄贈いただいた作品の展示方法について、ご相談させていただきたく存じます。
lines.en: Mr. Kiryu, I'd like to consult you about how we display the work you so kindly donated.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 何か問題でもありましたか。
lines.en: Has there been some problem?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 実は、戦時中の場面を描いたあの絵について、一部のお客様から不快だというお声が寄せられておりまして。
lines.en: The fact is, some visitors have told us they find the painting of a wartime scene upsetting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 不快、ですか。あの絵は、戦争の悲惨さを後世に伝えるために描かれたものです。見たくないものを隠すようなまねは、描いた父も望まないでしょう。
lines.en: Upsetting? That painting was made to convey the horror of war to future generations. My father, who painted it, would never want it hidden just because people don't like to look.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ごもっともでございます。私どもも、展示を取りやめるつもりは毛頭ございません。
lines.en: You are quite right. We have not the slightest intention of withdrawing it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: では、どうなさるおつもりですか。
lines.en: Then what do you intend to do?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 作品の隣に、制作当時の時代背景と作者の意図を説明するパネルを設け、入口にも注意書きを掲示してはどうかと考えております。
lines.en: We're thinking of placing a panel beside the work explaining the historical background and the artist's intent, and posting a notice at the entrance.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 説明を加えることで、かえって見る人の解釈を縛ってしまうのではありませんか。
lines.en: Won't adding an explanation actually constrain how viewers interpret it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そのご懸念はもっともです。ですので、解説は事実関係にとどめ、評価は見る方に委ねる形にしたいと存じます。
lines.en: That concern is well founded. So we would keep the text to the facts and leave judgment to the viewer.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: それならば、異存はありません。文面は事前に拝見できますか。
lines.en: In that case, I have no objection. May I see the wording beforehand?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: もちろんでございます。来週中に案をお送りいたします。
lines.en: Certainly. We will send you a draft within next week.

questions.question: What does the curator propose?
choices: Moving the painting to a less visible room
Keeping it on view with factual context and a notice
Adding the curator's own interpretation beside it
Returning the painting to the donor's family

questions.question: What is the donor's worry about the explanatory panel?
choices: It might tell viewers what to think
It might draw attention away from the painting
It might upset visitors even more
It might misstate his father's intentions

questions.question: What does the donor ask for before agreeing fully?
choices: A meeting with the visitors who complained
A larger space for his father's work
Removal of the notice at the entrance
A chance to review the text in advance

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 週休三日制の導入については、会社としても前向きに考えております。
lines.en: As a company, we are also considering the introduction of a three-day weekend positively.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。ただ、確認させていただきたいのは賃金の扱いです。
lines.en: Thank you. What I'd like to confirm, though, is how wages will be handled.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 労働時間が二割減る以上、給与もそれに応じて調整せざるを得ない、というのが経営側の考えです。
lines.en: Management's view is that since working hours fall by twenty percent, pay has to be adjusted accordingly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: それでは実質的な賃下げです。組合としては到底受け入れられません。
lines.en: That is effectively a pay cut. The union cannot possibly accept that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: お気持ちはわかります。しかし、休みが増えて給与が据え置きでは、コストばかりが膨らんでしまう。
lines.en: I understand. But with more days off and pay left unchanged, costs alone would balloon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 試行した他社の例では、業務の無駄を見直したことで、生産性がむしろ上がったという報告もあります。
lines.en: Other companies that tried it have reported that productivity actually rose because they cut out wasteful work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それは承知しております。ただ、うちのように顧客対応が中心の部署では、そう一筋縄ではいかない。
lines.en: I'm aware of that. But in departments like ours that center on dealing with customers, it isn't so straightforward.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: でしたら、まず一部の部署で半年間試行し、生産性が維持できれば給与は据え置く、という形ではいかがでしょう。
lines.en: Then how about a six-month trial in some departments first, with pay unchanged if productivity is maintained?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: なるほど、結果を見てから判断するということですね。それなら取締役会にも諮りやすい。
lines.en: I see, so we decide after seeing the results. That would be easier to put to the board.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ただし、評価の基準は労使で事前に合意しておくことが条件です。
lines.en: On condition, however, that labor and management agree on the evaluation criteria beforehand.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 異論はありません。次回までに、試行の対象となる部署の案をお持ちします。
lines.en: No objection. By next time, I'll bring a proposal for which departments the trial would cover.

questions.question: What arrangement do the two sides reach?
choices: A company-wide switch with a twenty percent pay cut
A trial limited to customer-facing departments only
A partial trial, with pay kept if output holds up
A delay until more companies have tried it

questions.question: Why is the executive reluctant to keep pay unchanged?
choices: Other firms saw productivity fall

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ああ、検査の結果が出たんだったね。

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい。予想以上に進行していました。ご本人は、家族にはまだ言わないでほしいとおっしゃっていて…。

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: うーん、それは悩ましいね。本人の意思を尊重するのが原則ではあるけれど。

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ただ、今後の治療方針を決めるには、ご家族の協力が欠かせません。奥様は毎日いらしていますし、いずれ気づかれると思うんです。

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: では、ご家族にお伝えしてもよろしいでしょうか。

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: ご家族に心配をかけたくない、ということなのかもしれませんね。

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 疑っているわけじゃないのよ。ただ、構成も論の運び方も酷似していて、第三者が見たら盗用と受け取られかねない。

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 影響を受けたのは事実です。でも、学問は先人の成果の上に成り立つものですよね。

lines.speaker: A

lines.en: Exactly. That's why making clear where their ideas end and yours begin is the minimum courtesy.

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: A

lines.en: Listing the source once at the end isn't enough. Wherever you drew on it, state it each time. And your own argument is still weak.

lines.speaker: B

lines.en: So I leaned too heavily on the earlier research.

lines.speaker: A

lines.en: Yes. Standing on the shoulders of giants is fine, but it's pointless if you don't look at anything from up there.

lines.speaker: B

dialogues.title: Negotiating the wording of a joint statement

speakers.name: ベルナ代表
speakers.hint: diplomat, courteous, quick to propose alternatives

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 共同声明の第二項ですが、我が国としては「深い懸念を表明する」という表現は受け入れがたいと申し上げざるを得ません。
lines.en: On paragraph two of the joint statement, I must say that my country finds the phrase 'express deep concern' difficult to accept.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 貴国のお立場は承知しております。ただ、我が国の世論を考えますと、懸念にまったく触れない文面では国内の理解を得られません。
lines.en: We understand your position. However, given public opinion in my country, wording that doesn't mention concern at all would not win understanding at home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 「懸念」という言葉自体を排除せよとまでは申しておりません。「深い」という修飾が、特定の国を非難しているかのような印象を与えかねない、ということです。
lines.en: I am not saying the word 'concern' itself must go. The issue is that the modifier 'deep' could give the impression of condemning a particular country.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: なるほど。では「深い」を削る代わりに、「双方が」という主語を加えるのはいかがでしょう。「双方が懸念を共有する」とすれば、一方的な非難とは読めません。
lines.en: I see. Then instead of 'deep', how about adding 'both sides' as the subject? If it says 'both sides share concern', it can't be read as one-sided condemnation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 検討に値する案ですね。ただ、「共有する」ですと、我が国にも責任の一端があると認めたと受け取られる恐れがあります。
lines.en: That proposal deserves consideration. However, 'share' risks being taken to mean we've admitted our country bears part of the responsibility.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: では、「双方が懸念に留意する」ではいかがでしょう。
lines.en: Then how about 'both sides take note of the concern'?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 「留意する」であれば、踏み込みすぎず、かといって何も言っていないわけでもない。落としどころとしては妥当だと考えます。
lines.en: 'Take note' neither goes too far nor says nothing at all. As a compromise, I think it's reasonable.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: ありがとうございます。第三項の経済協力の部分は、原案どおりでよろしいですか。
lines.en: Thank you. Is the economic cooperation section in paragraph three all right as originally drafted?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そちらは異存ございません。ただし、最終的には本国の了承を得る必要がありますので、正式なお返事は明朝までお待ちください。
lines.en: We have no objection there. However, in the end we need our government's approval, so please wait until tomorrow morning for a formal reply.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 承知いたしました。では、今夜中に修正案をお送りします。
lines.en: Understood. Then we'll send the revised draft tonight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 井上さん、来週の会議で新商品の説明をしてもらいたいんだけど、どうかな。
lines.en: Inoue, I'd like you to explain the new product at next week's meeting. What do you think?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 私ですか。この企画を中心になって進めたのは、前田さんですが……。
lines.en: Me? But it was Maeda who led this project…

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 前田さんは来週、大阪に出張なんだよ。
lines.en: Maeda is on a business trip to Osaka next week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうなんですか。でも、私、人前で話すのがあまり得意じゃなくて……。
lines.en: Oh, really? But I'm not very good at speaking in front of people…

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 資料は前田さんが作ってくれたし、井上さんはデータのところをいちばんよく知っているだろう？
lines.en: Maeda has already made the materials, and you know the data part better than anyone, right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: はい、データは私が集めました。では、前田さんに内容を確認してから、準備します。
lines.en: Yes, I collected the data. Then I'll check the content with Maeda and prepare.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それから、会議は木曜日の予定だったけど、社長の都合で水曜日になったから。
lines.en: Also, the meeting was planned for Thursday, but it's been moved to Wednesday to suit the president.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 水曜日ですか。前田さんは火曜日から出張ですよね。
lines.en: Wednesday? Maeda leaves on the trip on Tuesday, doesn't he?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そうだね。じゃあ、今週中に一度練習して、私と前田さんに聞かせてくれる？
lines.en: That's right. So could you do a practice run this week for me and Maeda?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: わかりました。金曜日の午後でよろしいでしょうか。
lines.en: Understood. Would Friday afternoon be all right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: すみません、スマホの料金が高いので、安いプランに変えたいんですが。
lines.en: Excuse me, my smartphone bill is high, so I'd like to switch to a cheaper plan.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: かしこまりました。今、毎月どのくらいデータを使っていらっしゃいますか。
lines.en: Certainly. How much data do you use each month at the moment?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 家ではWi-Fiなので、外ではほとんど使いません。
lines.en: I use Wi-Fi at home, so I hardly use any when I'm out.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: でしたら、三ギガで月千五百円のプランがおすすめです。
lines.en: Then I'd recommend the 3-gigabyte plan at 1,500 yen a month.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 安いですね。でも、電話はよくかけるんです。孫とか、病院とか。
lines.en: That's cheap. But I make a lot of calls — to my grandchild, the hospital…

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: そのプランですと、通話は三十秒二十二円かかります。かけ放題を付けると、プラス千円です。
lines.en: On that plan, calls cost 22 yen per 30 seconds. Adding unlimited calling is 1,000 yen more.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 合わせて二千五百円ですか。今は七千円なので、それでもずいぶん安いですね。
lines.en: So 2,500 in total? I pay 7,000 now, so that's still much cheaper.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: はい。あるいは、五分以内の通話が無料になるオプションなら、プラス五百円です。
lines.en: Yes. Or there's an option that makes calls under five minutes free, for 500 yen more.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 孫とは長く話すから、五分じゃ足りないなあ。
lines.en: I talk with my grandchild for a long time, so five minutes isn't enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: では、かけ放題のほうが安心ですね。
lines.en: Then unlimited calling would give you peace of mind.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうしましょう。それでお願いします。
lines.en: Let's do that. That one, please.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: すみません、さっき三階のトイレに傘を忘れてしまったんですが。
lines.en: Excuse me, I left my umbrella in the third-floor restroom a little while ago.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: どのような傘でしょうか。
lines.en: What kind of umbrella is it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 紺色の長い傘で、持つところが木でできています。
lines.en: A long navy umbrella with a wooden handle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: 少々お待ちください。……今、届いているのは、紺色の折りたたみ傘だけですね。
lines.en: One moment, please… The only one handed in is a navy folding umbrella.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: 折りたたみじゃないんです。じゃあ、自分で見に行ってもいいですか。
lines.en: Mine isn't a folding one. Then may I go and look myself?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: もちろんです。ただ、清掃の者がもう片付けているかもしれません。
lines.en: Of course. However, the cleaning staff may already have cleared it away.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: そうですか……。これから駅で友達と会うので、あまり時間がないんです。
lines.en: I see… I'm meeting a friend at the station now, so I don't have much time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: それでしたら、こちらの用紙にお名前とお電話番号を書いていただければ、見つかり次第ご連絡いたします。
lines.en: In that case, if you write your name and phone number on this form, we'll contact you as soon as it's found.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: お願いします。でも、雨が降っているので、帰りはどうしよう……。
lines.en: Please do. But it's raining — how will I get home…

lines.speaker: A
lines.ja: よろしければ、一階の受付で傘をお貸ししております。次にご来店の際に返していただければ結構です。
lines.en: If you like, we lend umbrellas at the first-floor reception. You can return it on your next visit.

lines.speaker: B
lines.ja: それは助かります。じゃあ、これを書いたら一階に行きます。
lines.en: That's a big help. Then I'll go down to the first floor after filling this in.
